The objective of this spike is to produce a document that describes the two primary architectural patterns for integrating microVMs (e.g. libkrun, wslc, apple containers…) into the Podman ecosystem.

h2. *Usage Patterns to be Documented*

# *MicroVM as a Podman Machine Provider*
#* *Context:* Long-lived VM environment.
#* *Behavior:* The VM is initialized once and acts as a persistent host for multiple containers.
#* *Goal:* Investigate usage as a provider on Windows/macOS (e.g., libkrun as a new provider on Windows).
#* *Key Considerations:* Resource persistence, shared storage, and integration with {{podman machine}} commands.
# *MicroVM as a Container Runtime*
#* *Context:* Ephemeral, per-container VM.
#* *Behavior:* A short-lived VM is spawned for each {{podman run}} and destroyed immediately after the container is removed.
#* *Goal:* Re-evaluate runtime support (similar to previous Kata support) specifically for high-isolation use cases.
#* *Key Considerations:* Startup latency (boot time), storage mapping complexity and network isolation.

Two-day in-person hackathon (Wed-Thu June 4-5, Brno office).

*Goal:* Port Jenkins CI regression tests to Testing Farm / GitLab CI in the sustaining-engineering namespace for podman, buildah, and skopeo on a single RHEL-10 branch as an MVP.

*Participants (on-site):* Tomas Sedlacek (coordination), Jan Kaluza (tech lead), Jindrich Novy, Jan Rodak, JhonHonce.
*Remote:* Neil Smith (PO liaison), Dave Darrah (PO).

*Target repo:* gitlab.cee.redhat.com/sustaining-engineering/container-tools/src-git/

*Slack channel:* #brno-containertools-hackathon

*Acceptance Criteria (MVP for 2 days):*
* Jenkins CI jobs for podman, buildah, skopeo on RHEL-10 are audited and mapped
* At least one component has regression tests running via Testing Farm triggered from GitLab CI
* Results are visible (MR status, dashboard, or email)
* Process is documented for replication to other components and RHEL versions

Upstream description: {quote}h3. {anchor:issue-description}Issue Description
The Docker-compatible stats endpoint \({{GET /containers/\{id\}/stats}}) returns CPU usage data that produces inflated and unstable CPU% values for containers running inside a Podman pod, while {{podman stats}} \(which uses a separate code path) reports correct and stable values for the same containers. Standalone \(non-pod) containers behave correctly via both interfaces.

This was originally reported as a Beszel monitoring bug: henrygd/beszel#1953. Beszel reads {{cpu_stats}} and {{precpu_stats}} from the Docker-compat endpoint and applies the standard formula

{noformat}
CPU% = (delta_container_cpu / delta_system_cpu) * online_cpus * 100{noformat}
For containers inside a pod, this produces values inflated by a roughly constant \~3.5x factor against {{podman stats}}, with occasional large spikes.

h3. {anchor:steps-to-reproduce-the-issue}Steps to reproduce the issue

import sys,json,time

    delta_sys = d['cpu_stats']['system_cpu_usage'] - d['precpu_stats'].get('system_cpu_usage', 0)
    delta_cpu = d['cpu_stats']['cpu_usage']['total_usage'] - d['precpu_stats']['cpu_usage']['total_usage']
    pct = (delta_cpu / delta_sys * 6 * 100) if delta_sys > 0 else 0
    print(f't={time.time()-t0:.1f}s  delta_cpu={delta_cpu:>12,}  delta_sys={delta_sys:>13,}  CPU%={pct:6.2f}%')

Upstream description: {quote}h3. {anchor:issue-description}Issue Description
My Macbook restarts after 3 or 4 minutes when it was shutdown and a Podman machine was running just before shutting down the Mac. The same issue was reported in [Q&A|https://github.com/containers/podman/discussions/25307] but never answered.

h3. {anchor:steps-to-reproduce-the-issue}Steps to reproduce the issue

# Start up the Macbook
# Open a terminal window
# Start Podman machine with the command "podman machine start"
# Wait until the machine is started succesfully
# Stop Podman machine with the command "podman machine stop"
# Shutdown the Macbook \(Apple icon on the leftcorner of the screen \-> Shut Down...)

h3. {anchor:describe-the-results-you-received}Describe the results you received
It looks like the Mac has shutdown but after 3 or 4 minutes it is restarting When I log in, there is a message "your computer was restarted because of a problem", when I click details, this is the comment:
